title: Unramifiedness tested on geometric fibres for a locally finite type morphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each point $s\in B$, let $\kappa(s)$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(s)}$, and let $h_{\bar s}:Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$ be the geometric fibre morphism [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then $h$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if every $h_{\bar s}$ is unramified. Empty geometric fibres are allowed. No flatness, finite presentation, quasi-compactness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 02G8 (lemma-unramified-etale-fibres), with Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field) and Descent Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified) for passage between ordinary and geometric fibres

proof.text: Assume that $h$ is unramified. For every $s\in B$, the geometric-fibre morphism $h_{\bar s}$ is the base change of $h$ along the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}\to B$ defining the chosen geometric point. Unramified morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change, so $h_{\bar s}$ is unramified.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tags 02GA and 02G8; geometric-fibre definition

proof.text: Conversely, assume every geometric fibre is unramified and fix $s\in B$. Put $B_s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and let $h_s:Z_s=Z\times_BB_s\to B_s$ be the ordinary scheme-theoretic fibre. By the definition of geometric fibre, after choosing $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(s)}$ the given geometric fibre is the base change of $h_s$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B_s$. The latter field-extension morphism is an fpqc singleton covering, and unramifiedness descends along fpqc coverings; therefore $h_s$ is unramified.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02VM, together with Topologies Tag 022B and the ordinary/geometric fibre identification in Morphisms Tag 02G8

proof.text: Apply the field-fibre characterization to the unramified morphism $h_s:Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. It follows that $Z_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable algebraic extensions of $\kappa(s)$.

The morphism $h$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis, and every ordinary fibre has the disjoint-union description from step 3. The ordinary-fibre criterion of Tag 02G8(2) therefore implies that $h$ is unramified.

proof_origin.place: Tags 02G7 and 02G8, with Descent Tag 02VM and Morphisms Tag 02GA

split_report.summary: Checked the imported statement against Stacks Morphisms Tags 02G7 and 02G8 and Descent Tag 02VM. The statement is correct with locally finite type only; empty fibres and arbitrary non-quasi-compact bases are allowed. The proof first uses base-change stability for the forward implication. For the converse it descends unramifiedness from each algebraically closed geometric fibre to the ordinary fibre along the fpqc field extension, applies the field-over-a-base characterization (new node), and then applies the ordinary-fibre criterion (new node). No hypotheses were added or removed.
